lessons.title: Meet Scratch
lessons.topic: Scratch interface, blocks and stage elements

game.name: Real vs Fake
game.story: You are a shopper learning to spot fake products (tomato paste, rice, milk, noodles). Tap the fake one and Oga Sharp tells you why it is fake.

lessons.big: Scratch has four parts you must know: the Stage (where the game plays), the Sprites (the characters), the Blocks (the code pieces) and the Script area (where you snap blocks together).
steps: Download the starter file below and open it in Scratch.
Look at the Stage. This is Real vs Fake.
Find the sprite list under the Stage. Count the sprites. Can you find Tick and Cross?
Click a sprite, then open its Costumes tab. Each costume is a different picture.
The Script area is empty. That is on purpose. In the next weeks YOU will fill it.
lessons.turn: Write down 3 sprite names from the list and one thing each one will do in the game. Show your list to your trainer.
lessons.play: You are a shopper learning to spot fake products (tomato paste, rice, milk, noodles). Tap the fake one and Oga Sharp tells you why it is fake.

quiz.q: What is the Stage?
o: The place where the game happens
quiz.why: The Stage is the picture area where your game plays.

quiz.q: What is a sprite?
o: A character or object you can control
quiz.why: Sprites are the characters, buttons and things in your game.

quiz.q: Which of these is a MESSAGE (broadcast) used in Real vs Fake?
quiz.why: 'game over' is a message that sprites send to each other.

lessons.title: Your first blocks
lessons.topic: Scratch blocks and the green flag

game.name: Real vs Fake
game.story: You are a shopper learning to spot fake products (tomato paste, rice, milk, noodles). Tap the fake one and Oga Sharp tells you why it is fake.

lessons.big: Every script starts with a hat block. The most used one is 'when green flag clicked'. Today every sprite gets a tiny script: when the flag is clicked, hide. That way the game starts with a clean stage.
steps: Open the Step 1 file (the starter).
Click Tick. From the purple Events group drag 'when green flag clicked' into the script area.
From Looks, snap 'hide' under it.
Click the green flag. Tick disappears. You just ran code!
Do the same for the other sprites in the list below, or open the goal file to see them all.
lessons.turn: Make Tick hide when the flag is clicked, then add 'wait 1 seconds' and 'show' after the hide. What happens?
lessons.play: You are a shopper learning to spot fake products (tomato paste, rice, milk, noodles). Tap the fake one and Oga Sharp tells you why it is fake.

quiz.q: Which block starts a script when the green flag is clicked?
quiz.why: It is a purple Events block.

quiz.q: Why do we HIDE sprites when the flag is clicked?
o: So the game starts with a clean stage
quiz.why: We hide them now and show each one at the right time.

quiz.q: Which of these is a SPRITE in Real vs Fake?
quiz.why: 'Fake Milk' is a character or button on the stage.

lessons.title: Make it tell a story

game.name: Real vs Fake
game.story: You are a shopper learning to spot fake products (tomato paste, rice, milk, noodles). Tap the fake one and Oga Sharp tells you why it is fake.

lessons.big: A game is a story told in small parts. Each part ends with a message (broadcast) and the next part starts when a sprite hears it (when I receive). Today you build the first two parts: the Title screen and the Play button.
steps: Open the Step 2 file.
On the Stage, build the flag script: it sets the starting values and broadcasts 'show title screen'.
On Title and Play Button, build 'when I receive show title screen' then show.
On Play Button, build 'when this sprite clicked' then broadcast the next message.
Click the green flag, then click Play. The story moves on!
lessons.turn: Change the words the Title says, or add one more 'say' with your own sentence. Run it again.
lessons.play: You are a shopper learning to spot fake products (tomato paste, rice, milk, noodles). Tap the fake one and Oga Sharp tells you why it is fake.

quiz.q: What does 'broadcast' do?
o: Sends a message to other sprites
quiz.why: A broadcast is like shouting, 'Everybody, the next part is starting!'

quiz.q: Which block waits for a message?
quiz.why: 'When I receive' lets a sprite wake up when the message comes.

quiz.q: Which of these is a VARIABLE in Real vs Fake?
quiz.why: 'Score' is a blue variable box. The others are sprites.

lessons.title: Make sprites move

game.name: Real vs Fake
game.story: You are a shopper learning to spot fake products (tomato paste, rice, milk, noodles). Tap the fake one and Oga Sharp tells you why it is fake.

lessons.big: Sprites move with x and y. x goes left and right, y goes up and down. 'go to x y' jumps. 'glide' slides. 'change x by' walks. Movement makes a still picture feel alive.
steps: Open the Step 3 file.
Pick 3 sprites from the list below, for example Tick and Cross.
Build their 'when I receive' scripts: show, go to, say and wait, in the same order as the goal file.
Run the game after each sprite. If something is wrong, compare with the goal file.
You do not have to build everything. Build 3 sprites yourself, then open the goal file to see the rest.
lessons.turn: Make Tick move in a new way: change the x number in 'go to' or add 'change x by 10' inside a repeat. Write what changed.
lessons.play: You are a shopper learning to spot fake products (tomato paste, rice, milk, noodles). Tap the fake one and Oga Sharp tells you why it is fake.

quiz.q: Which block puts a sprite at an exact spot?
quiz.why: x is left-right and y is up-down.

quiz.q: To move a sprite to the right you ...
o: change x by a positive number
change y by a positive number
quiz.why: A bigger x means more to the right.

quiz.q: Which of these is a MESSAGE (broadcast) used in Real vs Fake?
quiz.why: 'show rice' is a message that sprites send to each other.

lessons.title: Keep the score

game.name: Real vs Fake
game.story: You are a shopper learning to spot fake products (tomato paste, rice, milk, noodles). Tap the fake one and Oga Sharp tells you why it is fake.

lessons.big: A variable is a box with a name that remembers a number. In Real vs Fake the variable 'Score' is one of them. 'set' puts a new number in the box. 'change by' adds to what is already there.
steps: Open the Step 4 file and click the green flag.
Open the Variables (blue) group. Find 'Score'.
Finish the game: build the last scripts from the list below.
Play to the end and watch 'Score' change.
Open the goal file and compare your game with it.
Timer lesson: in the blue-green Sensing group find 'timer'. It counts seconds by itself. Games in this path use a variable called Time with wait blocks, but the timer block does the same job.
lessons.turn: Challenge: add a Timer. Make a sprite say 'Time: ' joined with the timer after the game ends. Then try 'reset timer' at the start.
lessons.play: You are a shopper learning to spot fake products (tomato paste, rice, milk, noodles). Tap the fake one and Oga Sharp tells you why it is fake.
addons: RED IF block: IF Score = 4, Oga Sharp says PERFECT. ELSE he tells you to look at your Score.
GREEN LOOP: repeat 3 times, Oga Sharp grows and shrinks to celebrate. The same steps again and again.

quiz.q: What is a variable?
o: A box that holds a number or word and can change
quiz.why: Like a score board that changes as you play.

quiz.q: Which block adds 1 to Score?
quiz.why: 'change by' adds to the old number. 'set to' replaces it.

quiz.q: Which of these is a SPRITE in Real vs Fake?
quiz.why: 'Tomato Paste Fake Talks' is a character or button on the stage.

lessons.title: Touch and decide

game.name: Family Job Board
game.story: Tayo must do the right chores before Daddy comes home. Tap the right chore, avoid the wrong one, and Mum keeps the score.

scripts.hat: when I receive 'tayo washes the clothes'
when I receive 'tayo sweeps the compound'
when I receive 'tayo washes the plates'

lessons.big: 'If' asks a question. If the answer is yes, the blocks inside run. Touching is a great question: 'if touching sprite' lets your game know when two things meet, which is how scoring by catching, bumping or tapping works.
steps: You now work on a second game: Family Job Board. Open the Step 3 file.
Read the story: Tayo must do the right chores before Daddy comes home. Tap the right chore, avoid the wrong one, and Mum keeps the score.
Build the first half of the game from the list below, or as many sprites as you can.
Watch for scripts tagged 'if'. These are the red blocks.
Open the goal file and test it.
lessons.turn: Touch challenge: add a new script to Mum: forever, if touching Tayo then say 'Touched!' for 1 second. Then change it to add 1 to a variable.
lessons.play: Tayo must do the right chores before Daddy comes home. Tap the right chore, avoid the wrong one, and Mum keeps the score.

quiz.q: Which colour is the 'if' block?
quiz.why: Red blocks ask a question: 'if this is true, then do that'.

quiz.q: 'If touching Tick then change Score by 1'. When does the score go up?
o: Only when the sprite touches Tick
quiz.why: The 'if' only runs the inside blocks when the question is true.

quiz.q: Which of these is a VARIABLE in Family Job Board?
quiz.why: 'Score' is a blue variable box. The others are sprites.

lessons.title: Levels and characters

game.name: Family Job Board
game.story: Tayo must do the right chores before Daddy comes home. Tap the right chore, avoid the wrong one, and Mum keeps the score.

lessons.big: Good games have levels (steps that get harder or different) and characters with their own look. A loop (green) repeats blocks, which makes animation easy: repeat 10 [change size, wait] makes a bounce.
steps: Open the Step 4 file of Family Job Board.
Build the second half from the list below.
Find a loop in the finished game (a green 'repeat' or 'forever').
Try changing the repeat number. What happens to the animation?
Give one character a new costume or a new name.
lessons.turn: Make one character react when something happens: a repeat 3 bounce (change size by 10, wait 0.2, change size by -10, wait 0.2).
lessons.play: Tayo must do the right chores before Daddy comes home. Tap the right chore, avoid the wrong one, and Mum keeps the score.
addons: RED IF block: IF Score = 4, Mum says PERFECT. ELSE she says good try. The game checks the Score and chooses.
GREEN LOOP: repeat 3 times, Tayo grows, waits, shrinks. The loop does the same steps again and again.

quiz.q: What does 'repeat 10' do?
quiz.why: A loop saves you from placing the same blocks again and again.

quiz.q: Which block lets a character look different?
quiz.why: Costumes are the different pictures of one sprite.

quiz.q: Which of these is a MESSAGE (broadcast) used in Family Job Board?
quiz.why: 'tayo sweeps the compound' is a message that sprites send to each other.

lessons.title: Design your own level

game.name: Honest Scale
game.story: You sell goods at Mama T's shop. Weigh the order honestly, give full weight, and keep your customers' trust.

lessons.big: Now you design. This is your third game: Honest Scale. You will rebuild its start, then plan one new level or new character of your own.
steps: Open the starter file.
Rebuild the flag-hides scripts and the Title and Play parts. You did this before, it should be quicker now.
On paper, draw ONE new level or character idea for the game.
Write the rule: what must the player do to win this level?
Share the idea with a classmate.
lessons.turn: Write your level rule using 'if': 'If ___ then ___ else ___'. Use real names from the game, like Customer and Walker.
lessons.play: You sell goods at Mama T's shop. Weigh the order honestly, give full weight, and keep your customers' trust.

quiz.q: When you design a new level, what should you decide first?
o: What the player must do and how they win
quiz.why: A good level has a clear goal.

quiz.q: What does 'if / else' give you?
o: Two paths: one when true, one when false
quiz.why: If the question is true do one thing, else do the other.

quiz.q: Which of these is a SPRITE in Honest Scale?
quiz.why: 'Minus Button' is a character or button on the stage.

lessons.title: Buttons and feedback

game.name: Honest Scale
game.story: You sell goods at Mama T's shop. Weigh the order honestly, give full weight, and keep your customers' trust.

scripts.hat: when I receive 'customer got full weight'
when I receive 'mama t checks trust'

lessons.big: Buttons make a game interactive. 'When this sprite clicked' waits for a tap. Feedback (a sound, a tick, a message) tells the player what happened. A game with no feedback feels broken.
steps: Open the Step 3 file of Honest Scale.
Build the first-half scripts, especially the ones starting with 'when this sprite clicked'.
For each button, check: what does the player see or hear after tapping?
Add one sound or one 'say' where feedback is missing.
Compare with the goal file.
lessons.turn: Add feedback to one button: a 'say' message or sound, plus a change to a variable.
lessons.play: You sell goods at Mama T's shop. Weigh the order honestly, give full weight, and keep your customers' trust.

quiz.q: A button in your game needs which hat block?
quiz.why: This hat block runs when the player taps the sprite.

quiz.q: Why do we give the player feedback (say, sound, tick)?
o: So they know if they were right
quiz.why: Good games always answer the player.

quiz.q: Which of these is a VARIABLE in Honest Scale?
quiz.why: 'Wanted' is a blue variable box. The others are sprites.

lessons.title: Test, fix, show

game.name: Honest Scale
game.story: You sell goods at Mama T's shop. Weigh the order honestly, give full weight, and keep your customers' trust.

scripts.hat: when I receive 'customer got full weight'
when I receive 'mama t checks trust'
when I receive 'end of the day'
when I receive 'end of the day'

lessons.big: Professional makers test and fix. Today you finish Honest Scale, playtest it with a friend, and write down what to improve. Your finished game should use all four logic colours: blue Variables, red Conditionals, green Loops, purple Events.
steps: Open the Step 4 file and build the last scripts from the list.
Open the goal file and compare.
Playtest: ask a friend to play without help. Where do they get stuck?
Fix one bug or add one small improvement.
Get ready to show your game: say what each colour does in it.
lessons.turn: Finish this sentence for your trainer: 'In Honest Scale my blue variable is ___, my red if checks ___, my green loop repeats ___, and my purple event is ___.'
lessons.play: You sell goods at Mama T's shop. Weigh the order honestly, give full weight, and keep your customers' trust.

quiz.q: What do you do in a playtest?
o: Play, look for bugs, and fix them
quiz.why: Testing is how every real game gets better.

quiz.q: Which four colours should your best game use?
quiz.why: Blue, red, green and purple logic together make a full game.

quiz.q: Which of these is a MESSAGE (broadcast) used in Honest Scale?
quiz.why: 'customer got full weight' is a message that sprites send to each other.

lessons.title: Meet Scratch
lessons.topic: Scratch interface, blocks and stage elements

game.name: Race Against Rot
game.story: Your tomatoes are rotting fast! Choose how to store them, drive to the market in time, and earn the most money.

lessons.big: Scratch has four parts you must know: the Stage (where the game plays), the Sprites (the characters), the Blocks (the code pieces) and the Script area (where you snap blocks together).
steps: Download the starter file below and open it in Scratch.
Look at the Stage. This is Race Against Rot.
Find the sprite list under the Stage. Count the sprites. Can you find Farmer and Open Air Card?
Click a sprite, then open its Costumes tab. Each costume is a different picture.
The Script area is empty. That is on purpose. In the next weeks YOU will fill it.
lessons.turn: Write down 3 sprite names from the list and one thing each one will do in the game. Show your list to your trainer.
lessons.play: Your tomatoes are rotting fast! Choose how to store them, drive to the market in time, and earn the most money.

quiz.q: What is the Stage?
o: The place where the game happens
quiz.why: The Stage is the picture area where your game plays.

quiz.q: What is a sprite?
o: A character or object you can control
quiz.why: Sprites are the characters, buttons and things in your game.

quiz.q: Which of these is a MESSAGE (broadcast) used in Race Against Rot?
quiz.why: 'buyer pays' is a message that sprites send to each other.

lessons.title: Your first blocks
lessons.topic: Scratch blocks and the green flag

game.name: Race Against Rot
game.story: Your tomatoes are rotting fast! Choose how to store them, drive to the market in time, and earn the most money.

lessons.big: Every script starts with a hat block. The most used one is 'when green flag clicked'. Today every sprite gets a tiny script: when the flag is clicked, hide. That way the game starts with a clean stage.
steps: Open the Step 1 file (the starter).
Click Farmer. From the purple Events group drag 'when green flag clicked' into the script area.
From Looks, snap 'hide' under it.
Click the green flag. Farmer disappears. You just ran code!
Do the same for the other sprites in the list below, or open the goal file to see them all.
lessons.turn: Make Farmer hide when the flag is clicked, then add 'wait 1 seconds' and 'show' after the hide. What happens?
lessons.play: Your tomatoes are rotting fast! Choose how to store them, drive to the market in time, and earn the most money.

quiz.q: Which block starts a script when the green flag is clicked?
quiz.why: It is a purple Events block.

quiz.q: Why do we HIDE sprites when the flag is clicked?
o: So the game starts with a clean stage
quiz.why: We hide them now and show each one at the right time.

quiz.q: Which of these is a SPRITE in Race Against Rot?
quiz.why: 'Truck' is a character or button on the stage.

lessons.title: Make it tell a story

game.name: Race Against Rot
game.story: Your tomatoes are rotting fast! Choose how to store them, drive to the market in time, and earn the most money.

lessons.big: A game is a story told in small parts. Each part ends with a message (broadcast) and the next part starts when a sprite hears it (when I receive). Today you build the first two parts: the Title screen and the Play button.
steps: Open the Step 2 file.
On the Stage, build the flag script: it sets the starting values and broadcasts 'show title screen'.
On Title and Play Button, build 'when I receive show title screen' then show.
On Play Button, build 'when this sprite clicked' then broadcast the next message.
Click the green flag, then click Play. The story moves on!
lessons.turn: Change the words the Title says, or add one more 'say' with your own sentence. Run it again.
lessons.play: Your tomatoes are rotting fast! Choose how to store them, drive to the market in time, and earn the most money.

quiz.q: What does 'broadcast' do?
o: Sends a message to other sprites
quiz.why: A broadcast is like shouting, 'Everybody, the next part is starting!'

quiz.q: Which block waits for a message?
quiz.why: 'When I receive' lets a sprite wake up when the message comes.

quiz.q: Which of these is a VARIABLE in Race Against Rot?
quiz.why: 'Price ₦' is a blue variable box. The others are sprites.

lessons.title: Make sprites move

game.name: Race Against Rot
game.story: Your tomatoes are rotting fast! Choose how to store them, drive to the market in time, and earn the most money.

scripts.hat: when I receive 'farmer checks the money'

lessons.big: Sprites move with x and y. x goes left and right, y goes up and down. 'go to x y' jumps. 'glide' slides. 'change x by' walks. Movement makes a still picture feel alive.
steps: Open the Step 3 file.
Pick 3 sprites from the list below, for example Farmer and Open Air Card.
Build their 'when I receive' scripts: show, go to, say and wait, in the same order as the goal file.
Run the game after each sprite. If something is wrong, compare with the goal file.
You do not have to build everything. Build 3 sprites yourself, then open the goal file to see the rest.
lessons.turn: Make Farmer move in a new way: change the x number in 'go to' or add 'change x by 10' inside a repeat. Write what changed.
lessons.play: Your tomatoes are rotting fast! Choose how to store them, drive to the market in time, and earn the most money.

quiz.q: Which block puts a sprite at an exact spot?
quiz.why: x is left-right and y is up-down.

quiz.q: To move a sprite to the right you ...
o: change x by a positive number
change y by a positive number
quiz.why: A bigger x means more to the right.

quiz.q: Which of these is a MESSAGE (broadcast) used in Race Against Rot?
quiz.why: 'show title screen' is a message that sprites send to each other.

lessons.title: Keep the score

game.name: Race Against Rot
game.story: Your tomatoes are rotting fast! Choose how to store them, drive to the market in time, and earn the most money.

lessons.big: A variable is a box with a name that remembers a number. In Race Against Rot the variable 'Time' is one of them. 'set' puts a new number in the box. 'change by' adds to what is already there.
steps: Open the Step 4 file and click the green flag.
Open the Variables (blue) group. Find 'Time'.
Finish the game: build the last scripts from the list below.
Play to the end and watch 'Time' change.
Open the goal file and compare your game with it.
Timer lesson: in the blue-green Sensing group find 'timer'. It counts seconds by itself. Games in this path use a variable called Time with wait blocks, but the timer block does the same job.
lessons.turn: Challenge: add a Timer. Make a sprite say 'Time: ' joined with the timer after the game ends. Then try 'reset timer' at the start.
lessons.play: Your tomatoes are rotting fast! Choose how to store them, drive to the market in time, and earn the most money.

quiz.q: What is a variable?
o: A box that holds a number or word and can change
quiz.why: Like a score board that changes as you play.

quiz.q: Which block adds 1 to Score?
quiz.why: 'change by' adds to the old number. 'set to' replaces it.

quiz.q: Which of these is a SPRITE in Race Against Rot?
quiz.why: 'Sun-Dry Card' is a character or button on the stage.

lessons.title: Touch and decide

game.name: Naira Wise
game.story: Ada gets pocket money every week. Share it into Save, Spend and Give jars before the clock runs out and reach her goal.

scripts.hat: when I receive 'check if 3 weeks are done'
when I receive 'mum gives pocket money'
when I receive 'ada checks the week'
when I receive 'ada checks her kolo'
when I receive 'jars and 10 second clock start'
when I receive 'jars and 10 second clock start'
when I receive 'jars and 10 second clock start'
when I receive 'jars and 10 second clock start'

lessons.big: 'If' asks a question. If the answer is yes, the blocks inside run. Touching is a great question: 'if touching sprite' lets your game know when two things meet, which is how scoring by catching, bumping or tapping works.
steps: You now work on a second game: Naira Wise. Open the Step 3 file.
Read the story: Ada gets pocket money every week. Share it into Save, Spend and Give jars before the clock runs out and reach her goal.
Build the first half of the game from the list below, or as many sprites as you can.
Watch for scripts tagged 'if'. These are the red blocks.
Open the goal file and test it.
lessons.turn: Touch challenge: add a new script to Week Banner: forever, if touching Mum then say 'Touched!' for 1 second. Then change it to add 1 to a variable.
lessons.play: Ada gets pocket money every week. Share it into Save, Spend and Give jars before the clock runs out and reach her goal.

quiz.q: Which colour is the 'if' block?
quiz.why: Red blocks ask a question: 'if this is true, then do that'.

quiz.q: 'If touching Tick then change Score by 1'. When does the score go up?
o: Only when the sprite touches Tick
quiz.why: The 'if' only runs the inside blocks when the question is true.

quiz.q: Which of these is a VARIABLE in Naira Wise?
quiz.why: 'Kolo ₦' is a blue variable box. The others are sprites.

lessons.title: Levels and characters

game.name: Naira Wise
game.story: Ada gets pocket money every week. Share it into Save, Spend and Give jars before the clock runs out and reach her goal.

scripts.hat: when I receive 'jars and 10 second clock start'

lessons.big: Good games have levels (steps that get harder or different) and characters with their own look. A loop (green) repeats blocks, which makes animation easy: repeat 10 [change size, wait] makes a bounce.
steps: Open the Step 4 file of Naira Wise.
Build the second half from the list below.
Find a loop in the finished game (a green 'repeat' or 'forever').
Try changing the repeat number. What happens to the animation?
Give one character a new costume or a new name.
lessons.turn: Make one character react when something happens: a repeat 3 bounce (change size by 10, wait 0.2, change size by -10, wait 0.2).
lessons.play: Ada gets pocket money every week. Share it into Save, Spend and Give jars before the clock runs out and reach her goal.

quiz.q: What does 'repeat 10' do?
quiz.why: A loop saves you from placing the same blocks again and again.

quiz.q: Which block lets a character look different?
quiz.why: Costumes are the different pictures of one sprite.

quiz.q: Which of these is a MESSAGE (broadcast) used in Naira Wise?
quiz.why: 'new week starts' is a message that sprites send to each other.

lessons.title: Design your own level

game.name: The Great Owambe Budget
game.story: You are planning a big owambe party on a budget. Pick the cards you can pay for, and think carefully before you borrow.

lessons.big: Now you design. This is your third game: The Great Owambe Budget. You will rebuild its start, then plan one new level or new character of your own.
steps: Open the starter file.
Rebuild the flag-hides scripts and the Title and Play parts. You did this before, it should be quicker now.
On paper, draw ONE new level or character idea for the game.
Write the rule: what must the player do to win this level?
Share the idea with a classmate.
lessons.turn: Write your level rule using 'if': 'If ___ then ___ else ___'. Use real names from the game, like Time and Host.
lessons.play: You are planning a big owambe party on a budget. Pick the cards you can pay for, and think carefully before you borrow.

quiz.q: When you design a new level, what should you decide first?
o: What the player must do and how they win
quiz.why: A good level has a clear goal.

quiz.q: What does 'if / else' give you?
o: Two paths: one when true, one when false
quiz.why: If the question is true do one thing, else do the other.

quiz.q: Which of these is a SPRITE in The Great Owambe Budget?
quiz.why: 'Party Time Button' is a character or button on the stage.

lessons.title: Buttons and feedback

game.name: The Great Owambe Budget
game.story: You are planning a big owambe party on a budget. Pick the cards you can pay for, and think carefully before you borrow.

lessons.big: Buttons make a game interactive. 'When this sprite clicked' waits for a tap. Feedback (a sound, a tick, a message) tells the player what happened. A game with no feedback feels broken.
steps: Open the Step 3 file of The Great Owambe Budget.
Build the first-half scripts, especially the ones starting with 'when this sprite clicked'.
For each button, check: what does the player see or hear after tapping?
Add one sound or one 'say' where feedback is missing.
Compare with the goal file.
lessons.turn: Add feedback to one button: a 'say' message or sound, plus a change to a variable.
lessons.play: You are planning a big owambe party on a budget. Pick the cards you can pay for, and think carefully before you borrow.

quiz.q: A button in your game needs which hat block?
quiz.why: This hat block runs when the player taps the sprite.

quiz.q: Why do we give the player feedback (say, sound, tick)?
o: So they know if they were right
quiz.why: Good games always answer the player.

quiz.q: Which of these is a VARIABLE in The Great Owambe Budget?
quiz.why: 'Joy' is a blue variable box. The others are sprites.
